Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1458; unaccused, i.e. (by implication) irreproachable:--blameless.
BiblicalUsage: Deacons must first be proved and then found blameless, and an elder must be blameless, the husband of one wife, with faithful children. The word names the man against whom no charge can be laid, not a perfect man but one no one can fairly accuse.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for blamelessness in church office carries no system of its own; its standard is Paul's, that leaders must be men no honest charge can stick to.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
